newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, diffs steady, Oman done at -15.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, diffs steady, Oman done at -15.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Tuesday after the overnight rally in futures prices, with differentials mostly steady.
The only exception was Oman, which was heard traded at MPM -15 cents from a South Korean refiner to a major after previously being traded at MPM -5 cents.
Traders said they still considered the trade too firm in the wake of the Dubai/Oman differential narrowing to only $1.00 from $1.05 in May.
Traders said they expected buyers to hold off the market to wait for offers to drop to MPM -25 cents.
A trader said Oman was being offered on a Dubai related basis at Dubai +85/+90 cents.
Other Middle East grades were being offered, but no buyers were in sight.
Lower Zakum and Umm Shaif were offered at ADNOC +10 cents, but traders valued them lower at flat and +5 cents respectively.
Traders said buyers remained relaxed across the board after a wave of West African imports were traded last week for Asia.
Traders said they counted six very large crude carriers of West African grades traded so far for first-half May loadings, indicating they would arrive in June.
Minas crude traded into China again, traders said.
The 200,000-barrel deal was done at ICP +10 cents, in line with recent deals.
Paper Tapis gained around 20 cents, supported by the overnight futures gains. May Tapis paper was quoted at $20.10 to $20.30.
Brent continued to gain in late Asian hours with June up 28 cents at $18.62 in London.
